# γ_i and the second-order correction in EDM's stochastic sampler (Algorithm 2)

This document marks pages only at the start of each section, so the page numbers below are where the relevant section begins.

## How γ_i is defined

Algorithm 2 (Section 4, p. 6) defines γ_i piecewise:

- **γ_i = min(S_churn / N, √2 − 1)** if t_i ∈ [S_tmin, S_tmax]
- **γ_i = 0** otherwise

γ_i sets how much fresh noise is added at step i. The sample is raised to a higher noise level, t̂_i = t_i + γ_i t_i (line 5). Then noise with standard deviation √(t̂_i² − t_i²), scaled by S_noise, is added to get x̂_i (p. 6).

The text explains each part of the definition (Section 4, "Practical considerations," p. 6):

- **The [S_tmin, S_tmax] window.** Stochasticity is enabled only in this range of noise levels. This counters the drift toward oversaturated colors at very low and very high noise levels.
- **S_churn / N.** Inside the window, S_churn controls the overall amount of stochasticity.
- **The √2 − 1 clamp.** It ensures γ_i "never introduce[s] more new noise than what is already present in the image." My own arithmetic, not stated in the paper: γ_i ≤ √2 − 1 means t̂_i² − t_i² ≤ t_i².

The tuned values of S_churn, S_tmin, S_tmax and S_noise were found by grid search and are listed in Table 5 (Appendix E.2, p. 43).

## When the second-order correction is applied

The correction is applied **only when the next noise level t_{i+1} is non-zero**. On the final step down to t_N = 0, the sampler uses the plain Euler step from line 8 (p. 6).

When it is applied, the correction is:

- d′_i ← (x_{i+1} − D_θ(x_{i+1}; t_{i+1})) / t_{i+1} (line 10)
- x_{i+1} ← x̂_i + (t_{i+1} − t̂_i)(½ d_i + ½ d′_i) (line 11)

**A note on the extracted text.** Line 9 of Algorithm 2 reads "if t_{i+1} = 0 then." This is almost certainly a lost "≠" symbol from the PDF conversion; the document warns that symbols may be misread. Three points in the paper support reading it as ≠:

- The matching line in Algorithm 1 is annotated "Apply 2nd order correction unless σ goes to zero" (Section 3, p. 4).
- The text says "stepping to σ = 0 would result in a division by zero, so we revert to Euler's method in this case" (Section 3, p. 4). Line 10 divides by t_{i+1}, so it cannot run when t_{i+1} = 0.
- Algorithm 3 has the same garbled "= 0" test, followed by an "else … Euler step" branch. Appendix D.2 (p. 40) describes this as a "fallback to Euler step."

Check the PDF if you need to quote the exact symbol.
